exposure: gestational age at delivery (early term: 37-37 weeks, late term: 41-41 weeks, compared to 39-39 weeks)
cohort: The study included all low-risk singleton term (37 to 41 weeks) newborns delivered in a single tertiary university-affiliated medical center over a 5-year period.
finding: Early term delivery (37-37 weeks) in low-risk singletons is independently associated with an increased risk of various neonatal morbidities, including respiratory morbidity, unexplained jaundice, hypoglycemia, and NICU admission, whereas late term neonates primarily showed a higher rate of large for gestational date without significant increases in other severe complications.
